verdict: NOT REFUTED. I rebuilt the loop of 3872a1f2-plan.py in my own engine (not the replication lane's) and tried every plausible meaning of the row index; no reading is both tradable and able to reproduce the reported numbers. plan.py computes one risk multiplier b per row (line 52) from the equity, peak and cooldown left by the previous row and applies it to all three legs booked on that row (lines 59, 62-66). The legs are entered at three different times (KR 06:30 UTC, US day 13:30/14:30, US night 20:00/21:00), so a single per-row b can only be right for a leg entered at the row boundary. Reading A (KR night stored on its exit row) sizes the KR night with a b fixed 13.5-14.5 h after entry, at the US close inside the night; it is the only reading that reproduces the reports (v10 65.1/70.5/62.5/83.8 % against reported-implied 64.1/68.2/61.7/82.4 %; v11-A and v11-D within 2-3 %p). The innocent readings fall far short: KR night on its entry row (M, same as a KST-shifted table) gives v10 47.3/53.0/45.2/65.5 % and v11-A 36.1/27.2/32.3 %; both nights on entry rows (C) gives v10 41.6/42.9/35.4/48.9 %; tradable sizing as in v11_live.on_kr_close (T1) gives v10 36.5/43.8/35.9/52.7 % and v11-A 23.6/11.3/5.6 %. A placebo confirms the cause: once the part of each KR night explained by the US session inside it is removed (same mean), the literal and tradable engines converge. One fingerprint is not matched by reading A (v10 calendar 2022), and the original engines g2.py/uni.py are missing, so "the package used reading A" remains an inference from plan.py plus the numerical fit.

findings.title: Claim not refuted: only the look-ahead reading reproduces the reports
findings.detail: An independent engine transcribing plan.py lines 52-69 was run under every row-index reading. Reading A (KR night on its exit row, so the row-start b comes from the US close 13.5-14.5 h after KR entry) reproduces 10 reported window CAGRs across three strategies: v10 gap 1.4 %p, v11-A 2.0 %p, v11-D 2.8 %p, plus the v10 loss-year set 2011/2015/2018/2022. Reading M (KR night on its entry row, tradable for KR sizing; identical to a KST-shifted table) misses by 16 %p for v10, 50 %p for v11-A and 30 %p for v11-D. Reading C misses by 27-53 %p and tradable T1 by 27-68 %p. Even a diagnostic that lets b see the US night ending 7 h after KR entry reaches only 49.0 % for v10 on 2010-03 (target 64.1).

findings.title: No reading makes the single per-row b tradable for all three legs
findings.detail: plan.py line 52 computes b once per row from EA, peak and cd left by the previous iteration (line 69), and eff() multiplies it into Lk, Lon and Lid (line 59). Under reading A the row boundary is the US close of D-1: correct for the US night, stale but fine for the US day, and 13.5-14.5 h late for the KR night entered at 06:30 UTC D-1. Under reading M the KR b is known at entry, but the row-end snapshot then contains a KR exit 3-4 h after the US close that sizes the next US night, and the US legs compound on equity inflated by a KR night that happens later. Separate KR and US event rows are excluded by plan.py itself: lines 22, 78 and 100 use 252.5 rows per year, i.e. one row per trading date.

findings.title: The gain comes from the US session inside the KR night, shown without any engine
findings.detail: The KR night has correlation 0.585 with the US close-to-close inside it and -0.048 with the last one known at entry. When the inside session falls more than 2 %, the night averages -1.31 % (209 nights, sum -273 % against +202 % for all nights); conditioning on the last known session gives +0.22 %. In the literal loop the cooldown switched on after entry on 97 nights for v10 (mean -1.24 %) and 230 for PRESET_A (mean -0.92 %). A multiplier that is never above 1 raises the KR gross contribution from 15.3 to 20.8 %/yr (v10) and from 25.0 to 40.3 %/yr (PRESET_A); with b known at entry it is 10.6 and 9.2 %/yr. Example: the night of 2022-01-05 to 01-06 (-0.74 %) is halved by a cooldown triggered by the US session of 01-05, 8 h after entry.

findings.title: Placebo: without the inside-session dependence the literal and tradable engines agree
findings.detail: Each KR night had the component explained by the inside US close-to-close removed (beta 0.42, mean unchanged, correlation 0). For v10 the literal loop then gives 53.8/57.3/51.5/67.4 % against tradable 50.8/56.0/49.9/63.5 %. For PRESET_A it gives 51.1/49.4/41.4/60.2 % against 46.9/57.5/52.0/63.6 %, so the literal loop is no longer better. The 26-77 %p gap seen with real nights therefore comes from that dependence, not from any other difference between the two engines.

findings.title: The P&L base adds a second, smaller inflation
findings.detail: plan.py line 62 books x = EA*Lk*kon with EA already updated by the previous row's US session, which happened after the KR position was opened. With b fixed at entry this alone lifts v10 from 36.5 to 45.2 % (2010-03 to 2025) and v11-A from 21.8 to 34.6 %. Every combination that fits the v10 targets within 4 %p needs both this base and the late cooldown; the fully tradable combination is last, with a gap of 26.9 %p.

findings.title: The package's own text points to the same alignment
findings.detail: The v9 report states that the KR night is about 0.47 x the previous day's US intraday return plus about 14 %/yr. That is reproduced (beta 0.46, constant 14.3 %/yr) only with the US session inside the night; the session known at entry gives beta -0.04. The rule text uses the same word for the crisis flag the KR leg reads (the most recently confirmed, previous-day US close), and plan.py line 11 builds crk as crisis shifted by one row. Both crisis variants fit v10 equally (gap 1.4 %p); for v11-A and v11-D the late flag fits better (2.0 vs 4.1 and 2.8 vs 5.1 %p). Whether the gate is also late stays undecided.

findings.title: Data, cost and tax assumptions do not explain the gap
findings.detail: Each leg alone matches the package: KR-only gives 8.8 % (package 8.8 %), and v9-US gives 34.5 % with raw MDD -50.8 % (package 32.1 % / -50.8 % including the later crash, which would be a -37.4 % month). The surplus appears only when the legs share one b and one EA. For v10 alone, a tradable engine with zero cost and zero tax comes close to the reported windows (58.7/67.6/56.7/72.5 %), but the package demonstrably charges cost and tax (v9-US would be 51.7 % without them), and for v11-A the same engine reaches only 39.0/42.0/23.3/13.8 % against 85.9/74.5/84.5 %. Cost at 1.0x with tax gives v10 40.9 %.

findings.title: One fingerprint is not matched by reading A
findings.detail: Reported v10 calendar 2022 is -40 %. Reading A gives -24.6 % (-30.3 % with the crisis gate at the entry row; noise band -37.9 to -22.6 %), while T1 gives -39.4 %. v11-A 2022 (-52 %) is matched by every reading, and v11-D (-48 %) lies between A (-41 to -44 %) and T1 (-52.8 %). My US-only v8 for 2022 is -39.3 % against a reported -42.3 %, so part of this is data or path sensitivity. It does not rescue a tradable reading, which misses all window CAGRs, but it shows my reconstruction is not identical to the package's v10 engine.

findings.title: The uploaded live code implements the tradable convention
findings.detail: on_kr_close takes b from risk_multiplier(E, st.risk), where st.risk was written by the last on_us_close, and uses the equity at 15:30 KST and st.us_crisis_last. That is T1. On 2010-03..2026-10-07 T1 gives v10 37.2 % / -59.0 % and PRESET_A 19.2 % / -66.5 %, against US-only 42.3 % and 36.3 % / -54.7 %. The delivered program therefore cannot earn the back-tested KR-leg contribution, and under its own timing the KR leg lowers PRESET_A below US-only on every window.

open_issues: g2.py, uni.py and ext.py were not uploaded, so which row g2.scen stores the KR night on is inferred from plan.py's structure and the numerical fit, not read at the source.

Reported v10 calendar 2022 (-40 %) is not reproduced by the literal reading (-24.6 / -30.3 %); it coincides with the tradable figure (-39.4 %). Single years are path-sensitive around the cooldown threshold, but this is unexplained.
Whether the KR crisis gate is also taken from the US close inside the night is undecided: both variants fit v10; the late flag fits v11-A and v11-D somewhat better.
Everything before 2010-03 with a KR leg (1999-2026 48.9 % / 77.6 %, the 1986 and 1929 figures, and the plan.py pickles) could not be tested because the synthetic KR series is not in the package.
Our data ends 2026-10-07; the comparison strips the reports' own 2026 YTD figures and nothing after that date was checked.
The KR night is a two-ETF proxy (the package used three), and the v9 yearly check uses approximate BOK rates from memory; the fit bands were robust to 15 bp noise and to dropping the carry.

My US-only v8 yearly table matches the report with correlation 0.997 but differs by up to 26 pp in single years (2003, 2009, 2017), so the US legs are close to, not identical with, the package's engine.

Cutting the KR position in the KRX night session at the US close could not be tested (no night-session prices); it could only avoid the move after the US close, not the whole night that the loop rescales.
